KEYS — Warm EP Tone/Tremolo; Toy Piano Color/Decay; Tape Piano Age/Space; Soft Organ Tone/Rotary; Bell Keys Brightness/Release; Lo-Fi Keys Filter/Wow. DRUMS — Kick01 Tone/Decay; Kick02 Punch/Decay; Snare01 Tone/Snap; Snare02 Body/Noise; Clap Tone/Width; Closed Hat Tone/Decay; Open Hat Tone/Decay; Low/High Tom Tone/Decay; Rim Tone/Room; Shaker Tone/Decay; Perc Hit Tone/Space. concept-global-behavior.content: Everywhere: M1/M2 change the two named top-of-display params (turning opens temporary value overlay). M3 always master volume — never saved track level or sample amplitude. BACK tap leave/cancel/up; hold opens main menu from anywhere. UP/DOWN lists/rows; LEFT/RIGHT horizontal/cursor/discrete values; OK enter/toggle/confirm. A-D execute bottom labels (blank=noop). PLAY start/pause; while stopped begins at start. STOP stop+return to beginning; hold STOP all-notes-off panic. REC from stopped: count-in then record selected loop track; while playing: overdub; during record: leave record keep playback. TAP: 2+ taps set BPM; hold TAP toggles metronome. Keyboard playable on performance/edit unless modal. Pads trigger assigned sounds unless screen says LANE/PAD SELECT. Status bar: BPM + battery; play/record symbol; no USB/MIDI status in V1.
concept-global-behavior.title: Global control behavior

concept-hardware-front-panel.content: Permanent controls: Display (screens + contextual labels); M1 context param 1; M2 context param 2; M3 master output volume in V1; soft keys A-D (labels on screen); Pads 1-6 (performance; may become lane select); BACK/MENU (tap=back/cancel, hold=main menu); D-pad+OK (focus, values, enter, confirm); STOP (stop transport, playhead to start; hold=all-notes-off panic); PLAY (play/pause loop or pattern); REC (record; during playback enter/leave overdub); TAP (tap tempo; hold=metronome toggle); Keyboard (current keyboard sound); Onboard mic (sampler source; monitor off by default). M1/M2 preferred as endless encoders. Enclosure-level (not front-panel workflow): mic, power, charging, audio out. Product subtitle: POCKET SYNTH / SAMPLER (not MIDI).
concept-hardware-front-panel.title: Front panel control vocabulary

concept-library-rules.content: FACTORY: bundled read-only; edit always creates User copy; cannot delete factory assets. USER: saved sounds from edited factory, mic recordings, or imports. RECORDED/IMPORTED: filters inside User for mic vs import sources — not separate copies. FAVORITES: references to Factory or User; removing favorite never deletes sound. SOURCE AUDIO: stored once; multiple user sounds may reference with different trim/tune/EQ. DELETE: only when no project or user sound references item; destructive confirmation mandatory. EXPORT: user sample sources as WAV via browser download; Rendered Copy applies edits else Source Export original. STORAGE: persistent browser storage; show usage; warn before pressure causes recording failure.
concept-library-rules.title: Library rules (Appendix B)

concept-navigation-map.content: Hold BACK/MENU enters six areas: PLAY, LOOP, SOUND, MIX, PROJECT, SETTINGS. Branches: PLAY->Library->Sound Detail->Sound Edit/Pad Assign. LOOP->Tracks->Track Menu / Loop Options / Sequencer->Step Edit. SOUND->Sound Library / Sampler->Mic or File Import->Sample Editor->Save Sample. MIX->six-track level/pan mixer. PROJECT->list->Save/Save As/Rename/New. SETTINGS->Audio/Metronome/Display/Storage/Permissions/About. Fast workflows: Play a sound: Boot->PLAY->D LIBRARY->choose->OK->A USE KEYS. Record mic: Hold MENU->SOUND->D SAMPLER->A MIC->REC->STOP->edit->save. Import: Hold MENU->SOUND->SAMPLER->B FILE->D OPEN->edit->save. Make a loop: Hold MENU->LOOP->select track->REC->perform->REC exit overdub. Step program: LOOP->B SEQ->pad lane->arrows step->OK toggle. Save project: Hold MENU->PROJECT->B SAVE (+ text entry if naming).
concept-navigation-map.title: Six top-level areas and workflows

concept-persistence.content: GLOBAL SETTINGS: master EQ, limiter preference, metronome click, display, storage permission/status, mic permission cache. PROJECT: BPM, key metadata, keyboard sound, pad assignments, loop tracks, loop options, sequencer patterns, mixer, octave/hold/voice where appropriate. USER SOUND: source ref, trim, tuning/root, playback mode, envelope, EQ, filter/shape, FX, name/favorite. SOURCE AUDIO: mic take or imported file once; referenced by sounds/projects. RECOVERY: rolling autosave of session. FACTORY LIBRARY: read-only app assets. Browser: IndexedDB or OPFS for media/state; request persistent storage; file picker/download for import/export. Manual should not expose implementation names unless troubleshooting.
concept-persistence.title: Persistence (Appendix E)

concept-recording-behavior.content: NEW RECORD: REC while stopped starts selected track after count-in; becomes timing reference if no existing loop. OVERDUB: REC while playing adds pass; REC again stops adding, playback continues. REPLACE: if track mode Replace, next pass replaces after confirm/count-in. PLAY DURING REC ALL: all unmuted tracks audible. MONITORED: only tracks with Monitor ON. OFF: backing silent; metronome may play. UNDO: only most recent record/overdub — not library edits. METRONOME never in recorded audio. MIC SAMPLE MONITOR off by default (feedback). PAD/KEY MONITOR: always hear current performance while recording unless modal blocks input.
concept-recording-behavior.title: Loop recording behavior (Appendix D)

concept-screen-01.content:
Screen 01: Boot / audio-engine initialization.
GET THERE: Appears automatically after power/app launch.
HARDWARE: No performance input is accepted until loading completes. STOP may still be treated as a panic command if the engine is partially initialized.
WHAT IT DOES: No sound is produced until the audio context is ready. When initialization finishes, CASSIO enters PLAY using the last project or an empty project.
SAVE/STATE: Last-open project ID and recovery state are read from local persistent storage.
NOTES: If audio initialization fails, CASSIO should show an error instead of silently entering PLAY. 6 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-01.title: Screen 01: Boot / audio-engine initialization

concept-screen-02.content:
Screen 02: PLAY - performance home.
GET THERE: Boot completes, or hold MENU -> PLAY.
HARDWARE: M1 = preset-defined Tone macro. M2 = preset-defined FX macro. M3 = master volume. A = octave down. B = octave up. C = Hold. D = open Library. Keyboard plays current sound; pads trigger assigned pad sounds.
WHAT IT DOES: Octave shifts keyboard notes by 12 semitones. Hold sustains released notes. M1/M2 alter the active sound in real time. Pad audio is independent of the keyboard sound.
SAVE/STATE: Selected keyboard sound, octave, Hold state and user edits are stored in the current project. Temporary macro movement becomes part of the sound state only when saving a user sound/project.
NOTES: Factory presets can be performed immediately. The current project key is metadata in V1 and does not force notes into a scale. 7 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-02.title: Screen 02: PLAY - performance home

concept-screen-03.content:
Screen 03: Main menu.
GET THERE: Hold BACK / MENU from any normal screen.
HARDWARE: UP/DOWN moves through PLAY, LOOP, SOUND, MIX, PROJECT and SETTINGS. OK opens the highlighted area. BACK closes the menu. Transport stays active.
WHAT IT DOES: Opening the menu does not change the sound. Existing loop or sequencer playback continues unless STOP is pressed.
SAVE/STATE: No state is saved merely by opening or navigating the menu.
NOTES: This is the main future-proofing mechanism: new software screens can be added later without new hardware. 8 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL

concept-screen-05.content:
Screen 05: Sound Detail.
GET THERE: From Sound Library, highlight a sound and press OK/More, or open the current sound's detail action.
HARDWARE: A = use on keyboard. B = edit. C = assign to a pad. D = favorite/unfavorite. M1/M2 remain live so the sound can be auditioned.
WHAT IT DOES: Use Keys makes the sound the main pitched instrument. Assign maps it to one of the six pad slots. Edit opens non-destructive user parameters.
SAVE/STATE: Favorite status and pad/key assignment are project/library metadata. Editing a factory preset never overwrites factory content.
NOTES: Factory samples that are intended as one-shots may still be assigned to the keyboard; the root note defines pitch mapping. 10 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-05.title: Screen 05: Sound Detail

concept-screen-06.content:
Screen 06: Sound Edit - Shape.
GET THERE: Sound Detail -> B EDIT. A selects Shape page.
HARDWARE: M1 = cutoff/brightness. M2 = resonance. LEFT/RIGHT or OK can change discrete voice/drive options shown in the lower rows. A/B/C/D jump between Shape, Envelope, EQ and FX pages.
WHAT IT DOES: Cutoff removes or reveals high-frequency content. Resonance emphasizes frequencies around the cutoff. Voice/drive options can make a sound more focused, saturated or mono/poly depending on preset type.
SAVE/STATE: Edits remain pending until BACK; then Save Sound is shown. Factory sources require Save As.
NOTES: Parameter names can vary by factory preset, but V1 should prefer musically obvious controls rather than exposing raw synthesis internals. 11 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-06.title: Screen 06: Sound Edit - Shape

concept-screen-07.content:
Screen 07: Sound Edit - Envelope.
GET THERE: Sound Edit -> B ENV.
HARDWARE: M1 = Attack. M2 = Release. A/B/C/D switch edit pages.
WHAT IT DOES: Short Attack produces a sharp immediate onset; longer Attack fades into the note. Short Release stops quickly; longer Release creates a tail after the key is released.
SAVE/STATE: Values are saved with a user sound or project sound state.
NOTES: V1 deliberately uses a simple two-control envelope here. More detailed ADSR controls can be added later as digital-only pages. 12 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-07.title: Screen 07: Sound Edit - Envelope

concept-screen-08.content:
Screen 08: Sound Edit - EQ.
GET THERE: Sound Edit -> C EQ.
HARDWARE: M1 = Bass, from -12 dB to +12 dB. M2 = Treble, from -12 dB to +12 dB. OK can reset the selected band to 0 dB; a Reset action may reset both.
WHAT IT DOES: Bass boosts/cuts low frequencies using a low-shelf EQ. Treble boosts/cuts high frequencies using a high-shelf EQ. This changes timbre, not note pitch or tempo.
SAVE/STATE: EQ values are stored with the user sound or current project sound state.
NOTES: Recommended implementation: low shelf around 120 Hz and high shelf around 6 kHz. Keep enough headroom/limiting to avoid clipping after boosts. 13 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-08.title: Screen 08: Sound Edit - EQ

concept-screen-09.content:
Screen 09: Sound Edit - FX.
GET THERE: Sound Edit -> D FX.
HARDWARE: M1 = Reverb amount. M2 = Delay amount. M3 still controls master volume.
WHAT IT DOES: Reverb adds room/space. Delay adds repeating echoes synchronized or free-running according to preset defaults. At 0% the corresponding effect is bypassed.
SAVE/STATE: Values save with a user sound. Factory preset changes require Save As.
NOTES: Detailed delay time, feedback or reverb type can be later digital pages; V1 only needs the two immediate musical amounts. 14 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-09.title: Screen 09: Sound Edit - FX

concept-screen-10.content:
Screen 10: Save Sound.
GET THERE: Press BACK from Sound Edit after modifying a sound.
HARDWARE: A = cancel and return to editing. B = edit name. C = Save As. D = Save when editing an existing user sound. Factory sounds disable overwrite and require Save As.
WHAT IT DOES: Saving does not alter playback except that the edited sound becomes a reusable library item.
SAVE/STATE: User sound stores a reference to its source plus filter/envelope/EQ/FX settings; factory media stays untouched.
NOTES: This non-destructive model prevents accidental loss and keeps factory content immutable. 15 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-10.title: Screen 10: Save Sound

concept-screen-11.content:
Screen 11: Pad Assignment.
GET THERE: Sound Detail -> C ASSIGN.
HARDWARE: Press a physical pad or use arrows to choose Pad 1-6. OK assigns the current sound. A clears the selected pad. B switches pad playback mode where allowed. C previews. D finishes. M1/M2 can set pad level/pan if shown.
WHAT IT DOES: Assigned pads become independent one-shot/gate/loop triggers during performance. Clearing removes the mapping but never deletes the sound from the library.
SAVE/STATE: Pad assignments save in the project. Optional per-pad level/pan save with the assignment.
NOTES: Pads remain performance triggers on PLAY and LOOP; the sequencer explicitly repurposes them as lane selectors. 16 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-11.title: Screen 11: Pad Assignment

concept-screen-12.content:
Screen 12: Sampler Home.

UI (from mockup): SAMPLER home. Options: Record from onboard mic (selected), Import from file system, Open user sample. Note: new recordings/imports enter same sample editor. M1/M2 preview tone/FX, M3 volume. Soft keys A MIC, B FILE, C OPEN, D BACK.

WHAT IT DOES: No audio changes until a source is recorded/imported. Existing project playback may continue behind the sampler unless the user stops it.
SAVE/STATE: New recordings/imports are staged until the user reaches Save Sample.
NOTES: Microphone and imported sources enter the same editor, so the manipulation workflow is consistent. 17 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
GET: THERE           MENU Hold    ->->SOUND MENU    SOUND to-> Sampler. open the Sound Library, then press D = SAMPLER.

concept-screen-13.content:
Screen 13: Microphone Record.
GET THERE: Sampler Home -> A MIC.
HARDWARE: REC starts recording after the configured count-in; STOP ends the take; PLAY auditions the last take. M1 = digital input gain. M2 = record threshold when threshold mode is enabled. B toggles count-in. C toggles monitoring. D saves/continues after a take.
WHAT IT DOES: The mic signal is captured into an audio buffer. Monitoring is OFF by default to prevent speaker feedback. Input gain changes recorded level; it does not change microphone hardware sensitivity.
SAVE/STATE: The take remains temporary until Save Sample. A staged take can be replaced by pressing REC again.
NOTES: On first use, the browser may request microphone permission. The onboard mic is the default/only V1 input source. 18 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-13.title: Screen 13: Microphone Record

concept-screen-14.content:
Screen 14: Import File.
GET THERE: Sampler Home -> B FILE.
HARDWARE: D = open system file picker. A = cancel. B displays supported formats. C can show recent imports. After the native picker returns a file, CASSIO decodes it and opens Sample Edit.
WHAT IT DOES: Importing does not alter the original file. CASSIO makes its own local working copy/reference and previews it through the same sound engine.
SAVE/STATE: The imported source is staged until Save Sample, then persisted in local app storage.
NOTES: Guaranteed V1 targets should be WAV and MP3. OGG and M4A/AAC can be accepted where the browser decoder supports them. The native file-picker UI itself is provided by the operating system/browser, not CASSIO. 19 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-14.title: Screen 14: Import File

concept-screen-15.content:
Screen 15: Sample Edit - Trim.
GET THERE: After mic recording/import, or open a user sample -> Edit -> Trim.
HARDWARE: M1 moves sample Start. M2 moves sample End. LEFT/RIGHT scroll the waveform; UP/DOWN zoom. A plays the selected region. B normalizes. C opens Sample Tools. D goes to Tune.
WHAT IT DOES: Only the selected region is heard when the sample is triggered. Normalization increases or decreases gain so the peak reaches a safe target without changing tone.
SAVE/STATE: Trim points and normalization metadata are saved with the user sample. Source audio remains intact.
NOTES: Keep Start before End; enforce a minimum playable region to prevent invalid edits. 20 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL
concept-screen-15.title: Screen 15: Sample Edit - Trim

concept-screen-16.content:
Screen 16: Sample Tools.
GET THERE: Sample Edit - Trim -> C TOOLS.
HARDWARE: A normalize, B reverse, C reset sample edits, D back. UP/DOWN can highlight the same actions and OK confirms.
WHAT IT DOES: Normalize changes level only. Reverse plays the selected source region backward. Reset returns trim/reverse/normalization state to the original imported/recorded source.
SAVE/STATE: Tools remain non-destructive metadata until the sample is exported/rendered. Reset is therefore safe.
NOTES: Destructive deletion is never placed on this screen; sample deletion lives in the library/storage workflow and requires confirmation. 21 CASSIO / V1 COMPLETE OPERATING MANUAL

concept-sound-engine.content: TONE/CUTOFF: darker low / brighter high harmonics. RESONANCE: boost around cutoff. ATTACK: time to full level. RELEASE: fade after key release. BASS EQ: low-shelf ~120Hz -12..+12dB. TREBLE EQ: high-shelf ~6kHz -12..+12dB. REVERB: wet amount. DELAY: amount; timing may follow tempo/preset. SAMPLE START/END: region in source buffer. NORMALIZE: peak to safe max, no compression. REVERSE: play region backward. COARSE/FINE TUNE: playback rate — pitch and duration move together in V1 (no pitch-preserving stretch). ROOT NOTE: keyboard note for base pitch. ONE-SHOT: plays to end. GATE: plays while held. LOOP (sample): repeats region until release/stop. TRACK LEVEL: non-destructive loop track volume. PAN: L/R. SWING: delay alternating seq subdivisions. GATE (SEQ): note duration relative to step.

concept-v1-boundaries.content: NO MIDI CONTROL: no external MIDI dependency; front panel self-contained. PITCH/TIME: sampler tuning changes playback rate (pitch+duration together); pitch-preserving stretch later. DEEP SYNTHESIS: musical macros not full osc/mod matrix. MORE TRACKS: V1 fixes loop/mixer to six. TOUCH: no core workflow requires touch; native browser dialogs are only host UI exceptions. Hardware can be frozen: all V1 tasks reachable with display, M1/M2/M3, A-D, pads 1-6, BACK/MENU, nav cluster, transport, mini keyboard.

finding-crash-persist-storm.content:
Debug session 397b28 (Sep 2026). iPhone Safari page silently reloaded while turning knobs in LOOP. Runtime evidence: 710 "persist recovery" writes in one phone session, bursts up to 55/s on loop-tracks/loop-menu/sample-edit, each serializing 8.19 MB of track PCM (bufferToStored copies Float32 arrays, then IndexedDB structured-clones again). No window.error / unhandledrejection / pagehide preceded the reload (Hypotheses A JS error, D boot failure, E backgrounding REJECTED; B memory/IDB storm CONFIRMED) — consistent with WebKit's memory watchdog killing the tab.
Fix: app.js #persist() debounced (600 ms trailing) with #persistNow(); flushPersist() on pagehide/visibility hidden (cassio_controller). LoopEngine.serialize() caches stored PCM per buffer identity (#storedAudio; seeded from applyState) so level/pan/fx edits never re-copy audio. Verified headless: 60 rapid knob ticks → 1 write.
Rule of thumb: never call #persist from knob/tick handlers without coalescing; keep large PCM out of hot paths.

finding-fx-library-sample-track.content:
Shared FX library for samples and loop tracks (Sep 2026).
- audio/fx_params.js: single registry of ~100 params in ordered groups (MIX, SAMPLE, PITCH, LOOP, AMP ENV, TONE/EQ, FILTER, SATURATION, LO-FI, TAPE/ANALOG, VINYL/NOISE, DEVICE, REVERB, DELAY, MODULATION, AMP MOD, DYNAMICS, STEREO, PERFORM/GLITCH, CHARACTER). Each param: key/type/min/max/def/fmt/scope ("s" sample, "t" track, "st" both). Helpers: fxDefaults, sanitizeFx, nudgeFx (knob), stepFx (◀▶), fmtFx, fxKnob01, resolveFx (CHARACTER macro overlays lerped by charAmt), syncSeconds.
- audio/fx_chain.js FxChain: input→preGain(gain)→[noise inject]→filter→filterDrive→sat→grit(bits/downsample/dropout/skip; lazy ScriptProcessor)→bass/mid/treble→tilt→device(bp+shaper wet/dry)→chorus/flanger(mod delay)→phaser(4 allpass)→tremolo→autopan→comp→limiter→M/S width(+swap)→level→pan→out, plus own reverb send (generated impulse per type/size/decay, tone LPF) and delay send (sync/free, feedback, ping-pong, clean/lofi/tape). Wow/flutter/vibrato exposed via attachRateMod(playbackRate). Noise generators (hiss/static/dust/crackle/hum) built lazily and gated by setActive().
- voices/sample.js SampleVoice rewritten on FxChain: trim, fades, ADSR (ampAttack/ampDecay/ampSustain/ampRelease), pitch (root/tuneSemis/fine/octave/detune/speed/bend), reverse (cached reversed buffer), loop fwd/rev/pingpong (segment chaining w/ crossfade), stutter (bpm-synced slice), mono/retrigger/choke groups, tapeStart ramp, tapeStop(), per-trigger randStart/randPitch/randPan/randReverse. Sample output goes through chain → engine.dry (so loops still record it). Legacy fields kept: gain, trimStart/End, tuneSemis, padMode, reverb, delay, bassDb, trebleDb.
- Key collisions with synth sanitizePatch avoided by naming: ampAttack.. (not attack/release), tilt (not tone). patchFromSound() seeds samples with fxDefaults so old saved samples don't inherit synth defaults (e.g. release 0.48). #applyProjectPatch no longer leaks synth project values into samples.
- Loop tracks: LoopEngine creates one FxChain per track (dest engine.master, never re-recorded); mute/solo gate on chain.input; t.fx persisted in loop state; setTrackFx(id,key,val). Track sources get wow/flutter rate mod.
- UI: screens/settings_list.js collapsible list shared by SAMPLE EDIT and new loop-fx screen (LOOP → track OK → "FX / SETTINGS…"). LEVEL is row 0; knobs follow the cursor (group header → first 3 params; param row → it + next two). M3 is only borrowed when a third param exists; else falls through to master. OK on header expands/collapses, on action row runs it (TRIM→CROP, NORMALIZE, TAPE STOP), otherwise previews. finding-loop-d2-step-sequencer.content:
LOOP D2 — Step Sequencer, implemented Sep 2026.

MODEL (store.js): project.seq = { current: "A".."D", patterns: { A..D } }. Pattern = { length: 16|32|64, swing 0..1, gate 0.05..1 (default 0.5), lanes: 6 × steps[length] }. Step = { on, vel (def 0.85), accent (vel→1.0), tie (extends gate into next on step), shift (-0.5..0.5 step), gate (null = pattern gate, or per-step override) }. defaultSeq/sanitizeSeq/sanitizePattern/sanitizeStep; SEQ_PATTERNS/SEQ_LENGTHS/SEQ_LANES exports. Included in defaultProject and saveRecovery (`seq`); restored at boot via stepSeq.applyState(). Lane N = pad N: sound is whatever project.pads[N] is assigned, so kit switch re-voices the pattern.

ENGINE (audio/step_sequencer.js): StepSequencer(transport, trigger). 50 ms setTimeout lookahead loop, 0.25 s lookahead, absolute times from transport._origin: stepSec = beatSec/4; odd 16ths delayed swing*stepSec*0.5; plus step.shift*stepSec. Pattern wraps every `length` steps so step 1 = bar 1 of loop tracks. Per due step calls trigger(lane+1, { when, velocity, gateSec, step, accent }); gateSec = (tiedSteps-1 + gate)*stepSec. Trigger callbacks fire ~40 ms before `when` so voices schedule exactly. start(origin)/stop()/resync(origin)/playheadStep()/onStep(i, lanes) for LED flash. Smoke test: onsets within 1–3 ms of expected at 120 BPM.

TRIGGER PATH (app.js): #padSound(n) → {slot, assigned, patch} shared by #padDown and #triggerPad(n, {when, velocity, gateSec}). #triggerPad never touches heldPads/HOLD; drums ignore gate; gate-mode samples and synth pads get noteOff(midi,false,{when: when+gateSec}). Voices: drum/glass_poly/sample noteOn(..., {when}) use t = max(ctx.currentTime, when); glass_poly/sample noteOff(..., {when}) use setTargetAtTime for future releases so the in-flight attack isn't cancelled. Output goes down the normal pad path (engine.dry) so a running pattern is recordable into a loop track.

TRANSPORT WIRING: #transportPlay → stepSeq.start(origin); #transportStop → stepSeq.stop(); REC startRecAt → stepSeq.start(startTime) alongside loopEngine.startPlayback; tap-tempo resyncFromNow → stepSeq.resync(transport._origin).

UI (seq_controller.js + screens/sequencer.js, SEQ_SCREENS = sequencer|step-edit): Entry LOOP track view soft key B "SEQ…" → seqCtl.open(); BACK/D → loop-tracks. Grid 6×16 per page; arrows move cursor (◀▶ wrap across pages), ▲ from lane 1 reaches header row where ◀▶ switch pattern A–D; OK toggles step (on release; hold OK 380 ms → Step Edit via app._okHoldTimer in #handleAction); pads 1–6 select lane (no audition); M1 swing, M2 gate, M3 master. Soft keys: A PAGE (cycles 16-step pages), B LENGTH 16→32→64→16 (extend by repeating pattern, truncate when shrinking), C SHIFT mode (◀▶ rotate lane ±1 step; C/OK/BACK exits), D CLEAR lane via confirm screen (confirmAction "clear-seq-lane"). Step Edit: M1 velocity, M2 per-step gate, ◀▶ micro-shift ±5%, ▲▼ step, A OFF, B ACCENT, C TIE, D/OK done. Playhead: seqCtl.startPlayheadLoop() rAF toggles .playhead on [data-seq-col] cells in place; render() only on structural changes. Pad LEDs flash via app.seqFlash + #onSeqStep. CSS: .seq-grid/.seq-row/.seq-cell.on/.accent/.tie/.lane-sel/.cursor/.playhead/.beat, .seq-header.selected.

VERIFY: /tmp/cassio_smoke/seq_smoke.mjs (headless Chrome CDP, portrait emulation, https://127.0.0.1:3000): programs kick 1/5/9/13, asserts onsets, wrap, length/page cycling, hold-OK → step-edit, tap toggle, header pattern switch, shift rotate, pad lane select, clear confirm, persist round-trip, synth-lane gate path.

finding-loop-record-overdub-fix.content:
Fix (Sep 2026) for perceived loop record "feedback/compounding" when keyboard overdubbing while tracks play.

ROOT CAUSE (investigated): Not audio-graph feedback — loop tracks route to master only, recTap taps dry bus only (verified: 220Hz backing → 0 energy in silent overdub capture). Real bug was phase misalignment: REC-while-playing used engine.now() instead of next loop boundary, so overdub passes were mixed into loop-aligned buffers at wrong offsets → flam/doubling each cycle felt like compounding.

P0: transport.nextLoopBoundary(origin, loopSec, now) — REC while playing snaps capture start to next downbeat; toast "REC @ NEXT LOOP" when wait >80ms.

P1: project.loop.playDuringRec = all|monitored|off (default all). Loop Options row + soft key C cycle. During capture loop_engine.#audibleWhileRecording: off=silent backing, monitored=tracks with monitor true, all=unmuted backing (still respects mute/solo).

P2: Recording track always silent during capture (#audibleWhileRecording returns false for _recTrack) — prevents hearing old take while laying new material.

Immediate input.gain.setValueAtTime(0) when muted during record (not slow ramp).

VERIFY: bin/smoke-loop-record (test/smoke/loop_record.mjs) — bleed test, alignment peak <500ms, playDuringRec off → rec+backing gain 0.
